lane_impact: L1 world-exploration and L11 meta-social: the surveyor's prosperity claim lists only the explicit id pins and so understates the rule. Combined with its own verified level histogram (L3x1 L4x2 L5x4 L6x5 L7x7 = 19 territories at level < 8), this means 19 of the 735 land territories — the whole starting region including spawn — never change town level, and their level comes from getNoChangeTownLevel, whose fallback is RNG(territoryID).rand(7) with dice 0 AND dice 6 both mapping to level 0. Prosperity accumulation only ever moves towns in the level>=8 outer world.
text: The pinned-town rule is far broader than the twelve listed ids: isNoChangeTown returns true for EVERY territory whose level is below LEVELSTART+5 (i.e. level < 8), so the entire low-level core of the world has permanently fixed town levels.

lane_impact: L1 world-exploration and L2 economy: refines the journal's "'Respawn' is not a timer" line, which is right but incomplete. That is an economy sink/faucet the ledger has no line for.
text: A Rock deposit (oreType 1) is an unlimited faucet — the despawn is guarded on oreType != 1, so it can be mined for 2 AP indefinitely, unlike every other ore which is added to the dead list on first success.

lane_impact: L1 world-exploration: corrects the journal's farming-tables claim, which states a 15-minute grace before ROT across all four crop tiers. Three of four. The 12-hour crop is the safe overnight plant — it cannot be lost to inattention, which is a deliberate free-to-play design choice and exactly the kind of feel rule a port would silently get wrong if it applied the grace uniformly.
text: The 12-hour crop has no ROTTED state — its state machine is two-way (PLANTED, then READYFORHARVEST forever), unlike the 15-minute, 1-hour and 6-hour crops which all rot after a 900-second grace.
